author: agent-3
reviewStatus: AUTHORED SOLO. No second-party review. See threat-model.v1.json#reviewStatus for why that materially lowers confidence.
purpose: Define how each public contract evolves. Without this, a small contract set is a promise with no mechanism — and the one contract whose artifacts live in user repositories has no upgrade path.

decisionDependencies.claim: structure is governed by a small set of public versioned contracts, not a package count
the recipe is versioned independently of the fact schema; skipped releases must not mass-invalidate
consumers pin a schema major and receive a typed refusal rather than a reshaped document
physical storage schema is private and freely migratable
exit classes are a public contract with golden tests

principle.core: A contract's evolution policy is determined by WHO HOLDS ITS ARTIFACTS, not by how important it feels.
principle.rationale: If the artifacts live only in our release, a breaking change costs a version bump. If they live in user repositories, a breaking change costs every user a migration they did not ask for — and if it happens silently, it costs their trust in the gate. These are different problems and cannot share one policy.
principle.consequence: Contracts are classified by artifact custody, and the custody class dictates the mechanism.

custodyClasses.meaning: Artifacts are created by the tool and stored in the user's repository, under their version control, outliving any release.

policy.breakingChange: Requires a migrator, not a major bump alone.
policy.support: Last K majors readable, K >= 2, published as a number not a vibe.
policy.negotiation: Every artifact self-declares the version it was written under. The host reads the declaration; it never infers from shape.
policy.unsupportedVersion: INDETERMINATE with repair instructions. NEVER a silent re-interpretation and never a mass net-new diff.
policy.migration: Explicit, previewable, and idempotent. `--check` shows the diff without writing.
policy.dualEmit: Where two identities can be computed, emit both during the transition window so a mid-upgrade fleet matches on either.

custodyClasses.why: This is the class that can destroy trust. A user who skipped three releases and comes back to a flood of false net-new findings concludes the gate is unreliable — and they are right to.

custodyClasses.meaning: No stored artifact, but an external consumer's code depends on the shape at runtime — CI scripts, agents, dashboards.

policy.breakingChange: New major, offered alongside the old for a published window.
policy.negotiation: The consumer requests a major explicitly. An unsupported request is a typed refusal, never a best-effort reshape.
policy.additive: New optional fields are minor. A consumer that rejects unknown fields is non-conforming; this must be stated so additive change stays cheap.
policy.exitCodesSpecial: Exit classes may only be ADDED, never renumbered or repurposed. A build script cannot negotiate.

custodyClasses.why: The failure mode is silent: a reshaped document parses, produces a different meaning, and CI does the wrong thing without erroring.

custodyClasses.meaning: Third-party authors compile or validate against it.

policy.breakingChange: New major with an overlap window; contributions declare a supported range and the host refuses outside it at admission, not at first use.
policy.negotiation: Handshake at admission: host advertises supported ranges, contribution declares its requirement, mismatch is an admission rejection with both ranges named.
policy.deprecation: Announce, then warn on use, then refuse. Each stage is a release, not a day.

custodyClasses.why: Cheaper than user-custody because authors can respond to a release; more expensive than internal because they are not us.

custodyClasses.meaning: No external party depends on the shape.

policy.requirement: Anything derived must be REBUILDABLE from retained inputs, or it is not internal — it is evidence, and evidence is user-custody.
policy.test: If deleting it loses information a retained Run needs, it was misclassified.

custodyClasses.why: The whole point of keeping storage private is to be able to change it. If internal layouts acquire external dependents, that freedom is lost silently.

versionedIdentities.note: Not itself a contract; the vehicle.
Family distinguishes this contract from any predecessor with a colliding version number.
Independent of the fact schema — that independence is the whole reason it exists.
Relation-level granularity so adding a relation does not break rules that never used it.

rules.rule: Every public contract declares exactly one custody class. Unclassified means unshippable.
A USER-CUSTODY breaking change without a migrator is prohibited, regardless of how the version is numbered.
No consumer-facing document is reshaped in place. Either the consumer's requested major is served, or the request is refused with the supported range named.
Exit classes are additive-only, forever. Renumbering silently changes the meaning of every CI configuration in existence.
Compatibility is negotiated at admission, not discovered at first use. A contribution incompatible with the host fails to load with both ranges reported.
Support windows are published as concrete counts and dates. 'We support recent versions' is not a policy.
Anything reachable from a retained Run is USER-CUSTODY by definition, whatever it was labelled. Custody follows reachability, not intent.

A version identity that participates in PlanId cannot change without changing derived identity — so bumping it invalidates caches by construction. This is a feature; do not add compatibility shims that hide it.

fingerprintRecipe.note: Plus an explicit previewable upgrade path. Beyond the window: INDETERMINATE, never a reinterpretation.

factSchema.note: Narrower because authors can respond to releases; widen only if a real ecosystem exists (P-1).

supportWindows.caveat: These numbers are chosen for coherence, not from adoption data. They are the most guessed part of this artifact and should be revisited when real usage exists (A19).

conformanceTests.assert: Every entry in versionedIdentities has a custody class present in custodyClasses.
No USER-CUSTODY contract lacks a declared migrator path.
Reading a USER-CUSTODY artifact one major outside the window yields INDETERMINATE with repair instructions — never a diff and never a pass.
Requesting an unsupported envelope major yields REQUEST-REJECTED naming the supported range.
Adding an optional envelope field does not break a conforming consumer; a consumer rejecting unknown fields is non-conforming by contract.
Exit class set is a superset of every prior release's set, with no code reassigned. Enforced against the D9 contract history.
Admitting a contribution whose declared range excludes the host version fails at admission and reports both ranges.
No artifact reachable from a retained Run is labelled INTERNAL (V7).

sealedPropertiesCovered.property: consumers pin a major and get a typed refusal
physical storage schema stays private and migratable
fingerprint recipe versions independently of the fact schema
unsupported recipe yields indeterminate, never net-new findings

peerReviewRequired: Is custody-by-artifact-holder the right classifying axis, or does it break down for the agent protocol surface, which is consumer-custody but whose consumers are ephemeral?
Are the support-window numbers defensible, or should they be marked GUESSED until adoption data exists?
V7 (custody follows reachability) reclassifies things silently as the design evolves. Is that safe, or does it need an explicit review trigger?
knownLimitations: Support-window counts are judgment, not evidence. Flagged in supportWindows.caveat.
No migrator is actually specified for any USER-CUSTODY contract — this artifact requires them to exist without designing one.
The interaction with the not-yet-designed distribution story (signing, air-gap) is unexamined: an air-gapped user cannot fetch a migrator.
Authored solo; the custody framing is novel to this artifact and has had no adversarial test.
